assets.prompt: Whimsical miniature scene: tiny workers in blue overalls and hard hats polishing a giant pearly-white molar tooth, buffing it with cloths and small polishers until it gleams. Calm soft blue background, clean playful claymation-adjacent style, soft studio lighting, gentle continuous looping motion, no text.

what_went_wrong.when: 2026-07-30T13:42:57Z, on the balance check - before any generation was submitted
what_went_wrong.note: Worth being precise about: this was the MCP transport in front of the service, not the image model rejecting a prompt. It succeeded ~37 seconds later with no change to the request. A retryable 5xx on a metered API is not a reason to start editing prompts.

post_processing.stills_final: 179 KB for all three, measured on disk
post_processing.video_final: 3.0 MB, used as delivered - not re-encoded
note: The widely-quoted '179 KB' is the three WebP stills, not the whole
directory: with the video the assets are 3.18 MB. The video autoplays
muted behind a poster (hero-woman.webp), so the poster paints while the
video streams and nothing render-blocks - but it is still fetched
eagerly, with no preload=none. On a slow connection that is 3 MB the
visitor did not ask for, and it is the obvious next optimisation.
This step is not housekeeping. The campaign's pitch is 'your website is
slow', so a demo site that arrives slowly ends the conversation.
